title: The verdict a plan-review turn answers with
description: The structured answer `oneharness.plan-review.toml` validates every review turn against, and the whole contract between the reviewer and `orchestrator/plan_review.py`, which records a pass only when `passes` is true and records nothing at all otherwise. A finding *is* a refused criterion, so the outcome and the findings are one statement and this schema admits them only where they agree: a refusal carries at least one finding, so a reviewer can never refuse a task while naming nothing to correct, and a pass carries none, so a verdict can never clear a task while reporting criteria it refuses. Nothing beside those two fields: a reviewer that answered with its own commentary, a severity, or a rewritten task would have that extra silently ignored, so the schema refuses it here — where oneharness re-prompts — rather than downstream where nothing is watching. This file is hashed into every review key, so editing it invalidates every record made under the previous version; `just review-plan <source:project>` is what re-reviews an invalidated task, at one judged turn apiece.

passes.description: Whether this task's authored content may be dispatched. False records nothing, so the task stays refused by `just check-plan` until its content changes and is reviewed again.

findings.description: One entry per criterion this verdict refuses, and the only thing that says what to correct. Every entry is shown to the operator on its own line, so a task with three refused criteria is reported as three lines rather than as one — which is the whole reason a verdict carries a list. Empty on a pass.

criterion.description: The criterion this finding is about, quoted or named closely enough that its author can find it without re-reading the whole task. It has to carry a non-whitespace character, because a finding naming nothing leaves its reader exactly where a refusal carrying no finding at all does — and a run of spaces names nothing while satisfying a length. `minLength` and `pattern` are both declared so this file states that rule at the same strength `orchestrator/plan_review.py` reads it back at.

why.description: Why that criterion is refused. It names the criterion's own defect rather than an impression of the task, and carries a non-whitespace character for the reason `criterion` does.
